We agree.
speaker: Amyssa
Guild Master
Tonica
dialog: Trees are by far the most valuable and rare crop in the universe. More valuable than gold. What do you mean? There are trees everywhere. A tree provides other living things nourishments, housing, kindling in the winter, it is life preserving.
dialog2: Gold is but a coin of trade for the greedy. There's also gold everywhere, the stars sparkling out in the sky are filled with gold, but not even one tree. If the trees go scarce, no amount of gold will prove sufficient.
dialog3: I will return to my duty overlooking the pasture soon.

speaker: Tonica
dialog: Pardon me Innkepper, my duty is with the woods. I must fulfill my oath and remain the steward.

speaker: Hogperson

speaker: Tutorial
dialog: Located on a countryside road, it is far enough from the township to host travelers and close enough to attract local patrons.

speaker: Tutorial
dialog: You've recently come in contact with the lands governor, and applied to participate in establishing a safer environment for your business,

speaker: Tutorial
dialog: You have been offered partnership! You've signed a contract allowing you to host a guild of adventurers right here in your tavern.

speaker: Tutorial
dialog: This wonderful business enterprise will surely increase your revenue and your popularity among adventurers greatly! *Wink*

speaker: Traveler

speaker: Narrator
dialog: With this new found information, you consider it may be valueable to you, you carry on your way towards danger, and the captured traveler.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
Hogperson may not be the smartest guy, nor *A* smart guy, 
nor being able to appear smart if his life was depending on it, 
but he's got a big heart! And that counts.

Hogperson gains 50 Exp.

speaker: Narrator

dialog:

dialog:
You let Claudio out of the cage, catch up on what's been going on lately.

dialog:
You're all glad to have regrouped once again, and decide not to split up again,

then you carry on ahead on your way towards the Pot of Gold Bragain stashed for himself.

dialog:

dialog: Oooooh, Dad's gone? I wonder for how long. I hope he's alright.

speaker: Guild Master
dialog: Well since business have seem to be quiet down here.

speaker: Guild Master
dialog: How about you three will get on that case, I want you to head on East towards the township nearby, wouldn't be more than a day's walk.

speaker: Guild Master
dialog: There's a Tavern there just like this one, that's where you'll find Hogmother. You can assess the situation better once we know more.

speaker: Guild Master
dialog: There should be business proposals and contacts to make there, so keep me posted.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Well well, not a moment's rest.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The long winding road by the mountain and the more-mountains is your path, straight up ahead.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Argh, outdoors again. What I wouldn't give to be deep underground in my workshop surrounded by my clan again.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: That looks like some track! Hope it'll be safe...

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Wait up.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: You guys, hey wait!

dialog: Are you going to make me run???

dialog: It seems that Amyssa have took off from the Tavern on her own, and have followed in your footsteps...

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: I was thinking about this and I've came here because my conscious just doesn't allow me to relax back at the Tavern

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: It doesn't feel right at all!

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
I'm sorry about my behavior.
I ask for your forgiveness.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
You all may really be COMMONERS, ugh
but your cause is a NOBLE one.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Please allow me to join your party, it would bring me honor to serve alongside you.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: If you'll allow me, I will put all my might and magic into finding your father, Hogperson.

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Oh, there's nothing to feel sorry about, young lass. You are most welcome in our midst! I'm sure mother would love meeting you.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: You've shown your true colors Missa Myssa, hehehe.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Oh it's a pleasure to host a lady of stature such as yourself! Mi' lady, I, Claudio, am delighted to have you! Aaaand, I find your scrolls the labor of an artist.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: With your new member, the road carries on.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: As you're walking the unpaved road you notice a few silver coins scattered on the ground. How fortunate. You pick them up and carry on your way.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: You encounter a Red Deer grazing nearby. It's a large male with a full build of antlers, seems rather dangerous. It is grazing and neutral towards your arrival.

options.text: Leave and allow the beast to graze peacefully.
Avert from your path and attack the beast.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: You cross paths with a Dwarven fellow, he seems like a migrant away from his mountain home.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The Dwarven Migrant seems apprehensive to deal with strangers. He says he's carrying nothing but raw gemstones that aren't worth much more than a few coins. He is hoping to find a location when he could practice his Gem Cutting art.

options.text: [Pickpocket] Attempt to slip a gem off the migrant.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Your Appraisal adept strikes a conversation about the gem market with the Dwarf.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The dwarf migrant's eye widen at your knowledge. He says it's rather dangerous for him to wander alone and he've been dodging robbers left and right. He'd rather if you hold on to this gem. He hands you a speciality cut gem he've been hiding. It would be much safer with you.

You both part ways and carry on your journey.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The dwarf migrant appreciates your banter. He rewards you with a rough gem from his sack.

You both part ways and carry on your journey.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party passes through the Green Road, leading towards town. There are markings on the road, where it is forking to the south, signaling a shrine is locate there. Would you be interested to visit the shrine?

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Mother would be interested to visit the shrine for sure. Maybe she've passed through there too? Or we just might bump into her on our way there? I hope nothing bad happened and she didn't get stuck there.

options.text: Carry on your way towards town.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party will go to visit the shrine.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party will carry on the Green Road, leading towards town.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Heading out towards the shrine, the party paces through the unmarked path. It's a nice sunny day in the green pastured lands outside town. Your party's mood is upbeat, the shrine is visable from this point and it would take a short while to reach it.

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: That's it. Here we are. Wish mother was here, she knows all about shrines. It looks rather tidy and clean, maybe she was here recently.

options.text: Have a Dwarf inspect the stones of the shrine.
Carry on your way towards town.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Right! Rocks are my specialty. The place has been built by a mason, but it seems it was built hastily, the cuts on the stone are rather inaccurate and a bit shoddy. Perhaps they were more interested in marking this specific location rather than building a shrine of splendor. The green growth around the place seems to respect the sanctity of the place and not cover it. Not much for that statue over there, it's all covered with vines and ferns.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Why would that be, Bragain?

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Beats me, I'm no herbalist. They do look rather different than the rest of the greenery around. The statue stone is far different than the shrine stones, and there are no chistle markings on it, it must have been an entirely different mason to have sculpted it.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: After having said a quick prayer for the success of the journey, and the safety of Hogfather, the party heads back to the main path towards town.

speaker: Apparation
dialog: Halt Bragain!

speaker: Apparation
dialog: Stand fast Bargain of the subterranean miners!
dialog2: Why are you wasting your time with those ragged wanderers who get nowhere and accumulate nothing?!
dialog3: Come join me in the depths, surrounded by treasures we’ll be richer than all of them!

speaker: Bragain
dialog: What? … but where?!
dialog2: You’ll know where… find the vein and follow it through deep in the earth… I’m not far under the ground.

dialog: The apparition vanishes.
dialog2: What was that?! That was some wild fey spirit, ugh and I wasn’t even drinking anything.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The party has reached the Township Tavern.
The place is bustling, travellers and entertainment fill the air with they pressence.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: There's Hogmother right there! Sitting at her table!

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: MOTHER!!!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: HOGGY!!!

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The mother and son greet each other with a warm hug and kisses, and a quick word about the letter.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Well Hoggy what a wonderful surprise, I did not expect to see you here!

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Well mother, if dad's away nothing is too important to keep me from seeing to it.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh that's just splendide! And you've brought some friends along, what a pleasure to meet you all! Let me fill you in on what's been happening.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: It appears there's quite some unrest at town right now as a dangerous group have been taking up territory up north across the river, and folks have begone missing!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: I still don't quite know what's the offical authorities policy regarding that, word is they might have voluntarily went there to join with them.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: I certainly have no intention of sitting here waiting for anyone. I'm going right in there and find Hogfather!

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Right ma'. And I'm coming with you.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Aye, that seems like a mission to me. I'll be by your side madam.

speaker: Claudio
dialog: Oh it would be a opportunity I will not miss out on, you will have every ability in my satchel at your disposal madam Hogmother.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
And you will have my bow!

I mean, I don't have a bow, but, I am coming too!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh my! That's such a fortunate turn of events! I did NOT expect such a wonderful party! Hoggy, I've raised you so well! I am so proud of you!

speaker: Creature
dialog: Pardon me . . . . .

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Oh! Excuse me, yes?

speaker: Creature
dialog: It would be wise to not draw any further attention, would you join me out in the alley for further discussion?

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
What was that?!

That creature just popped out of nowhere.

He is now leaving through a side entrence amist the commotion of the tavern, rather unnoticed.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party throws surprised looks at each other, trying to process what just happened.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Hogmother is the first to stand up and follow the creature, the urgency of the case walks before her, and the party follows her outside.

speaker: Creature
dialog:
Ahem . . . . .

Excuse me for not introducing myself, but I've been eavesdropping on your conversation and couldn't participate in public.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: The name is Lurch, expert Reconnaissancer. My services might be of interest to you, if you're willing to listen to me.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Well this is very sudden, but, Master Lurch, we are in a predicament and are willing to hear you out.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: The group out in the woods are no strangers to me. Although I do not affiliate with them, I can walk in and out of their territory with no problem.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: And since you haven't attempted to hide your plans to simply waltz in there, I do not believe you are going to make it. Not without a lot of help.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Well, whether we do or we don't, *I* am going to find Hogfather. And I'm willing to hear your offer for help!

speaker: Lurch
dialog: I see, the presentation of my offer will have to remain mostly in secret, for my own safety, but I will provide you with support from behind the lines, with anything that might tackle you on your way.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: For my service I will request 200 silver coins.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Bah! I don't like this. That's a steep amount with nothing to show for? Your goblin-folk are all tricks and mayhem! This is a robbery!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: That's enough Master Dwarf.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: What?! How do you know he will not alert the enemy for our approach! I do not trust this Goblin for one bit!

speaker: Lurch
dialog: well then, the offer falls off the table! This villain can't be dealt with, he'll signal the enemy of the plan and have *me* hanged, just like that!

speaker: Bragain
dialog: There's nothing I'd like to do more, goblinoid!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: There'll be none of that! Not while Hogfather is in distress and not ever!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We are not traitors!!!

speaker: Narrator
dialog: It seems this meeting is about to come to an early end... would you?

options.text: Sternly refuse any further contacts with the Spy.
[Calm] Have hogmother Speak softly to Lurch and assert his safety is assured.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party has decided to leave the alley and abandon the dealing with the Goblin. They will head out immidatley towards the forest.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: I will cover that payment Master Lurch, and once Hogfather is safe I'll see to a bonus as well.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: I don't like this, but lives are on the line. I accept this offer and I'll cover in for your payment too, Lurch, as a token of good will.

speaker: Lurch
dialog: That settles it then. I shall leave immediately through the tunnels. From this moment forth, we have never met, and I will contact you in secret.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: That's it then. The deal has signed with handshakes and coin. I hope you know what you're doing dealing with Goblins!

speaker: INTRODUCTION
dialog: Lurch is a Spy, his speciality is espionage in hostile locations without raising suspicion. While his monsterous image may be vile, he's not the worst you can come across.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party will head out immidatley towards the forest now.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: I still have a bad feeling about this.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Oh dear Hommond, may the glory of your hammer protect us. I hope we're not waltzing straight to our doom AND our bankrupcy.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: NEVER trust a Goblin. That's what my folks always say

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: Or an elf

speaker: Bragain
dialog: OR AN ELF!

speaker: Bragain
dialog: Oh I mean, not ALL elves, not always

speaker: Amyssa
dialog:
............

That's alright. You're not the only one having second thoughts.

speaker: Amyssa
dialog: But lives are on the line here. There are greater matters ahead and it's no time to be picky.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party marches on.....

options.text: Tell Hogmother about the shrine you've passed through on your way here.

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Pardon me mother, on our way here we've passed through a shrine located next to the path, have you seen it by any chance?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: A shrine not far from the path, to the south?

speaker: Hogperson
dialog: Yes that.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Yes I have. Spent a bit of time there praying for advice on what to do. While waiting I cleaned and tidied up the place, but didn't get any answers I'm afraid, so I carried on.

speaker: Bragain
dialog: You've missed the statue then have ya'?

speaker: Hogmother

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: We aren't aligned with the Ugress. We're here to rescue my husband from this place.

speaker: Wormtail
dialog:
Not yet... The Ugress can be, very persuasive.

And I don't think you can stand up to her.

You're all going to fall for her spell, or die. If I let you go through my sewers, there's no coming back for you.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: The Forest rejects the influence of the Ugress in its midst. Master Awetruce aligned with us, he will face the Ugress.

speaker: Wormtail
dialog: She has armed troops everywhere, who is going to take on them?

speaker: Hogmother
dialog:
We'll go right now while the gate is open and the guards are outside, we'll allow Awetruce in and straight to her

If he succeeds, the spell will break.

speaker: Wormtail
dialog: This plan just might work. I harbor much hatred for this Ugress for taking up on my territory, I will take you to her. Hurry.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
In a feat of skill the wererat in his huge rat form zips through the sewers with tremendous agiliy. To your relief he is leading you forward.

The Maze of the sewers may appear daunting, but it's not much more than straight pipes going in a steady upwards slop, and connected logically.

Quickly, the giant rat reaches the final sewer cover, wide enough for all of you to fit in one by one. He looks up to the surface and inspects the inner grounds of the fort.

speaker: Wormtail
dialog: The Ugress will be in her main Den, her henchmen will be mostly in their huts, I will sneak by and seal their doors by my magic. You make your own way to the gate, and confront her directly.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The party exits the sewers, while the Wererat skittishly hopping between makeship huts, casting his magics. To your great fortune you see the central yard is mostly empty, and the main gate remains open.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Awetruce must be outside, all this commotion can't go unnoticed by the forest. I will see to him.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
Out the gate, in the bushes, sure enough the menacing face of the Direwolf and his piercing red glowing eyes are staring back at you.

It is the time to spring the trap. Face the Ugress directly in her Den.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The guards stationed at the Den are demanding of disposal.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Upon defeating the guards stationed at the Den, you are now ready to face your final adversary. The large wooden door of the main Den opens, It's the hidious Ugress herself, in a most flared mood, more than her usual unpleasant self.

speaker: Ugress
dialog: WHAT IS THE MEANING OF THIS?! GUARDS! AT MY COMMAND AT ONCE!

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: There are no guards, Ugress. You will face us now. I urge you to release the innocent folks you've charmed with your Geas, let them go this instance!

speaker: Ugress
dialog:
HOW DARE YOU! SMALL BARBARIAN, AT MY HOME?!

(beings chanting spell incantations)

POWERS OF MIGHT,
SPELLS OF ENCHANTING,
DELIVER THIS PEST,
INTO MY WEBLING.........................

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: MASTER AWETRUCE NOW !!!

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: AAAAAAAAAWWWWWWWWOOOOOOOOOO.....

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The Direwolf bolts past you faster than lightning, in direct collision towards the Ugress.

speaker: Ugress
dialog:
PATRON OF FIENDS,
THE FOREST AWOKE,
DAMN THIS WOLF,
CRUSH HIM TO PULP

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The Direwolf leaps on the Ugress. Right as she releases a bolt of vile energy in a green blast to his chest, and blows the wolf away.

Awetruce have been struck down, and lays to the side in a lifeless heap.

speaker: Ugress
dialog: YOU HAVE SUCH NERVE TO BE FACING ME YOU UNDERLINGS, I WILL RULE THIS LAND AND YOU WILL ALL OBEY MY COMMANDS!

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The Ugress is a fearsome warlock, but she've forgotten, Direwolfs don't just die in one fell swoop ..................

EVEN A DEAD WOLF'S HEAD CAN STILL BITE

speaker: Awotruce
dialog: AAAAAAAAAWWWWWWWWOOOOOOOOOO.....

speaker: Ugress
dialog: WHA.. WHA.. WHAAAAT!! . . . . . . . . .

speaker: A DIFFERENT, DEEPER VOICE
dialog:
INSIGNIFICENT WOLF . . . 

THIS NATURE NODE IS MINE ! ! !

speaker: Narrator
dialog: The Direwolf leaps again upon the surprised Ugress, ferociously biting into her, and tear her body apart, first he bites into her spellcasting arm, and tears it away, then bites into her neck, and tears her head off...

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Then the mighty Direwolf collapses to the ground... dead.

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The spell of the Ugress have lifted off the garrisoned troops.

Figures and faces pop out of the huts, slightly confused in their new state, is the Geas finally lifted?

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Hogfather appears out of a nearby hut.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: Hogfather!

speaker: Hogfather
dialog: Hogmother! You've came for me......................

speaker: Narrator
dialog:
The Hogcouple is united once again. Not much words could be exchanged at that moment. The party agreed to take Awetruce the shrine of Narlia, and also the Ugress head as offering to altar, thinking it would please the godess seeing the blight has lifted from her forest.

One of the captured folk, Marlnus have befriended Hogfather and have joined up with you. Marl is an old adventurer, now a carriagefarer. He offers his services as aid, and his carriage to help the party's logistics planning.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: Arriving at the shrine, the forest appears lively more than ever. The flowers are at full bloom, bird singing sounds everywhere. Bright light reflects of the shrines cold white stones. You lay Awetruce to slomber, and the Ugress' head on top of the altar.

speaker: Hogmother
dialog: I pray this offering pleases you godess, though it was heavy and sudden on all of us, only one had to pay the ultimate price. We will leave your forest now, fare thee well benelovent one.

speaker: Narrator
dialog: In this final note, the party with the company of Marlnus heads back to the Inn, Finnik to his village, Wormtail to his sewers, and Awetruce to his final rest.

speaker: Developer
dialog: End of current development.
